2.text: On the way ten Taˊn˙ñɪn warriors fell upon him; but he slew them all,

3.text: and took for himself their reindeer and one full set of arms, a suit of armor,

4.text: a spear, a bow, and a quiver. When he came to the rock and turned to

5.text: the right, he saw a young Chukchee man driving a reindeer-team. This one,

6.text: seeing upon the new-comer the weapons and dress of an alien tribe, turned

7.text: and fled. Taˊlo’s reindeer were very swift. Very soon he passed the Chukchee,

8.text: driver, and, wishing to talk with him, barred his way. The other one turned

9.text: and fled in another direction. Taˊlo again overtook him and caught hold of

10.text: the bridle of the right reindeer with his hand. The Chukchee threw down

11.text: the reins. “If I became like a wild reindeer for you, (then slay me!)”¹ —

12.text: “No, I do not want to slay you. But, tell me, who are you?” — “I am

13.text: Omrɪtaˊhɪn’s son. We were three brothers, but the middle one was taken

14.text: by the Taˊn˙ñɪt when very young.” — “Then I am your brother,” said Taˊlo.

15.text: “I was brought up by Taˊn˙ñɪt. My armor is alien, but the body under the

16.text: armor was borne by a white sea-woman.” Then they greeted each other, and

17.text: grew to have no fear of each other. “Where are your houses?” asked Taˊlo.

18.text: “Here, near by, hidden behind the hill.” — “How many tents?” — “Three

19.text: tents, — my brother’s and mine, then that of an old ‘neighbor in the camp.’” —

20.text: “Well, let us go there!” — “But I must go first. If you go before me,

21.text: they will kill you.” — “No, let me go first; otherwise they will say that an

22.text: enemy is pursuing you.” — “No, let me go! Whoever brings good news

23.text: must go on ahead.” So they go together, one sledge behind the other. They

24.text: drive very fast; and the reindeer of one sledge are all the time close upon

25.text: the reindeer of the other. When they began to get near the camp, the people

26.text: of the camp exclaimed, “A Taˊn˙ñɪn is pursuing our man!” Men with bows

27.text: appeared, and shot a quantity of arrows at Taˊlo. Even the snow-dust flew

28.text: upward as in a tempest. When the snow-dust settled down again, they saw

29.text: Taˊlo standing a little apart, quite safe, and dusting the snow from his clothes.

30.text: Then the brother told them. Taˊlo lived with his kinsmen, but the next year

31.text: he arranged a daring invasion into the Taˊn˙ñɪn land. He slew a great many

32.text: people, took fifteen herds and eighty young slaves. One night he came to

33.text: his father-in-law. “I want to tell you something,” says the old man. “You

34.text: take your wife and carry her to your land. As for us, better kill us with a

35.text: lance. We are too old to leave our native country and adopt the ways of

36.text: an alien tribe.” He slew the old people and left them on that very place,

37.text: with the tent and all their belongings.

38.text: Another part of this interesting tale, also very characteristic, will be given

39.text: in one of the next chapters.

41.text: against the Russian Cossacks, Yäkuˊnnin’s adopted son also figures, who fights
